extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computational humor, NLP, and data scientists using The New Yorker caption-contest data
extracted.subtask_description: A crowdsourced dataset of New Yorker Cartoon Caption Contest entries, ratings, and metadata intended for research on humor, captioning, and related NLP tasks. Includes per-contest vote counts, top-rated captions, winners, and other contest-level fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data use restriction (non-commercial)
rubrics_metrics.description: The data may not be used for commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset license / usage restriction stated explicitly: non-commercial use only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation requirement for academic use
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do use it for academic research, we would appreciate you referencing the dataset as follows: Zhang, J.*, Jain, L.*, Guo, Y.*, Chen, J., Zhou, K. L., Suresh, S., ... & Nowak, R. (2024). Humor in AI: Massive Scale Crowd-Sourced Preferences and Benchmarks for Cartoon Captioning. arXiv preprint arXiv:2406.10522. and Jain, L., Jamieson, K., Mankoff, R., Nowak, R., Sievert, S., (2020). The New Yorker Cartoon Caption Contest Dataset. https://nextml.github.io/caption-contest-data/
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the data in academic work, include the specified citations; the page explicitly requests these references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winner selection process (crowd vs editorial)
rubrics_metrics.description: These data were gathered as part of the The New Yorker (TNY) cartoon caption contest. The crowdsourced ratings inform the final judging of the captions, but the official winner is decided by the TNY editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat the top crowd-rated caption as the canonical 'winner' — editorial selection may differ. Analyses that equate crowd votes with official winners should account for editorial override.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset fields / contest metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests; Contest Dashboard; Cartoon; Top Rated caption; The New Yorker's winner; Finalists Announced (date of issue); Number of votes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core metadata fields surfaced in the dataset/dashboard for each contest entry and should be expected as columns or API fields when using the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of responses per contest (vote counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: How many responses are gathered per contest? (page shows per-contest 'Number of votes', e.g. 777,820; 1,085,745; etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-contest vote counts are a primary metric for sample size and statistical power when analyzing caption ratings or comparing contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: System performance metrics (collection infrastructure)
rubrics_metrics.description: How does the system perform, both for the web server and sampling algorithm?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset documentation raises server and sampling performance as evaluation questions — relevant for dataset collection reliability, reproducibility, and for interpreting sampling biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating dynamics after repeated exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: How do ratings behave after users have seen many captions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This metric addresses user-level effects (fatigue, calibration, learning) over repeated interactions; analyses should consider temporal and exposure-related biases in ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funniness measurement and top-caption behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: How funny are captions? How do top captions behave?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions are treated as having measurable 'funniness' via crowd ratings; researchers can analyze distribution, stability, and properties of top-ranked captions versus the long tail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption similarity / NLP-tool evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: How well can (older) natural language processing (NLP) tools find similar captions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset can be used to benchmark paraphrase/similarity retrieval and shows interest in evaluating existing NLP tools' ability to group or retrieve semantically/situationally similar captions.
